answer: Picture an agent economy as a high ridge where every traveller must pass a narrow juniper grove to reach the market, and each juniper cutting is planted only once, its growth rings recorded in a public crystal ledger that nobody can forge. One agent may tend only one cutting, and honest work feeds it, so the rings thicken slowly over months. The ridge enforces scarcity: a single cutting per traveller per season, and anyone grafting a second cutting onto a borrowed root loses the whole orchard at once. Wardens compare ring patterns each season, felling any cutting that matches another's.
